literal_source_claim_en: The theory of real closed fields.
statement_blocker: The catalog supplies a topic gloss rather than a proposition. Primary and authoritative leads distinguish a finite-algebraic-closure characterization, construction and uniqueness of real closures, the orderability/formal-reality criterion, and several equivalent real-closed-field presentations. The same theorem name also denotes a characteristic-p extension result. Selecting or conjoining any of these at intake would invent or substitute mathematics.
domain_and_universes: Open: the selected source must fix an abstract field or ordered field, its universe, any chosen ordering, algebraic extension or closure, embeddings, and the representation of algebraic closedness and finite degree.
conclusion: Open: the repository does not choose a finite algebraic-closure characterization, orderability criterion, real-closure existence or uniqueness theorem, or equivalent polynomial characterization.
candidate_scope_not_credited: a field is orderable if and only if -1 is not a sum of squares
a field with a nontrivial finite algebraic closure is real closed, with algebraic closure of degree two obtained by adjoining a square root of -1
a field is real closed if and only if adjoining a square root of -1 produces an algebraically closed field
an ordered field has an algebraic real closure, unique up to order-preserving equivalence over the base
semireality together with square-or-negative-square and odd-degree-polynomial-root conditions characterizes real closedness
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: an already algebraically closed base field
trivial, infinite, or nonchosen algebraic closure
-1 already a square or a sum of squares
multiple field orderings and compatibility of an extension ordering
uniqueness as a field equivalence versus an ordered equivalence over the base
excluded_substitutions: the characteristic-p Artin-Schreier classification of cyclic degree-p extensions by X^p - X - a
Tarski quantifier elimination, completeness, decidability, or model completeness for real closed fields
Hilbert's seventeenth problem, a real Nullstellensatz, or a concrete Real/Complex special case
the fields of IsRealClosed restated as the desired theorem
a structure or hypothesis that assumes the desired ordering, closure, equivalence, or algebraic closedness
generic semireal, ordering, polynomial, algebraic-closure, or finite-dimensional APIs alone
the catalog's untrusted verified label or the discovery probe as proof credit
